name: Arduino Uno R3
description: ATmega328P at 16 MHz with an ATmega16U2 USB bridge. 32 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM, 1 KB EEPROM, 14 digital I/O of which 6 are PWM, 6 analog inputs. 5 V logic. Official board; clones with a CH340 are much cheaper and drop the 16U2.
frame: Centre origin. +x points from the USB-B edge toward the DC barrel. +y points toward the digital headers; the analog and power headers are on the −y edge.
notes: Barrel jack is 5.5 × 2.1 mm. USB-B. Reset button near the USB connector.

name: Arduino Uno R4 Minima
description: Renesas RA4M1 (R7FA4M1AB3CFM), Cortex-M4 at 48 MHz, 256 KB flash, 32 KB SRAM. Same Uno shield outline as R3, with USB-C, a 12-bit DAC, CAN and an op-amp. 5 V GPIO. No radio.

pins.name: CANH
pins.fn: CAN high, on the extra header area

frame: Centre origin. +x points from the USB-B edge toward the DC barrel. +y points toward the digital headers; the analog and power headers are on the −y edge.
notes: Shield-compatible with R3. Some R4 documents round the length to 68.85 mm; the hole pattern matches R3.

name: Arduino Uno R4 WiFi
description: RA4M1 plus an ESP32-S3-MINI-1 for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE, a 12×8 red LED matrix and a Qwiic connector. USB-C. Same Uno outline and 5 V GPIO as the Minima.
frame: Centre origin. +x points from the USB-B edge toward the DC barrel. +y points toward the digital headers; the analog and power headers are on the −y edge.
notes: The ESP32-S3 is the network coprocessor. GPIO on the shield headers is 5 V from the RA4M1. Wi-Fi transmit current sits well above the 80 mA typical board figure.

name: Arduino Nano
description: ATmega328P at 16 MHz in the classic 45 × 18 mm Nano outline. Mini-USB, 5 V logic, two 1×15 headers on 2.54 mm pitch. 32 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM, 1 KB EEPROM. No mounting holes.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.fn: 3.3 V from the USB bridge regulator

frame: 45 × 18 mm. The two 15-pin rows are 15.24 mm apart (6 × 2.54). Mini-USB is on one short end.
notes: Official Nano uses an FTDI FT232. Most clones use a CH340 and a Micro-USB jack on the same outline.

name: Arduino Nano ESP32
description: Nano outline with a u-blox NORA-W106 (ESP32-S3). USB-C, 3.3 V logic — not 5 V like the classic Nano. Arduino lists 8 MB flash; the S3 has 512 KB SRAM. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE.
frame: Same 45 × 18 mm Nano footprint and 15.24 mm row spacing as A000005.
notes: Do not feed 5 V into a GPIO. VIN still accepts a higher supply through the onboard regulator.

name: Arduino Mega 2560
description: ATmega2560 at 16 MHz. 256 KB flash, 8 KB SRAM, 4 KB EEPROM, 54 digital I/O, 15 PWM, 16 analog inputs, 4 UART. USB-B, 5 V logic, 101.6 × 53.3 mm. Four Ø3.2 mm mounting holes; coordinates are on the Arduino mechanical drawing and are not copied here.
notes: End header opposite the USB connector carries the extra GPIO. ICSP is 2×3.

name: ESP32-DevKitC-32E
description: Espressif reference board for the ESP32-WROOM-32E with 4 MB flash. Dual-core Xtensa LX6 at 240 MHz, 520 KB SRAM, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Classic plus LE. Two 1×19 headers, Micro-USB, 3.3 V logic. PCB 54.4 × 27.9 mm. No mounting holes.

pins.name: IO0
pins.fn: Boot strap, hold low while resetting to flash

pins.name: IO21
pins.fn: Default I2C SDA on many Arduino builds

pins.name: IO22
pins.fn: Default I2C SCL on many Arduino builds

frame: 54.4 × 27.9 mm PCB. Headers run along the two long edges. Micro-USB is on one short end.
notes: Wi-Fi TX peaks can reach about 400–500 mA. GPIO 34–39 are input-only. The linked PDF is the WROOM-32E module datasheet.

name: ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 N8R8
description: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R8: dual LX7 at 240 MHz, 512 KB SRAM, 8 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE, native USB. Two headers of 22 pins. Official v1.0 boards use two Micro-USB jacks (UART bridge and USB OTG).

pins.name: GPIO48
pins.fn: RGB LED on later revisions; GPIO38 on v1.1

notes: Octal PSRAM uses GPIO 35–37. Confirm the LED pin against the board revision. Outline below is an estimate; use Espressif’s DevKitC-1 DXF for a case.

name: ESP32-C3 SuperMini
description: Tiny third-party ESP32-C3 board sold as “SuperMini”. Single RISC-V core at 160 MHz, typically 4 MB flash, 400 KB SRAM, USB-C, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE. Castellated edges. There is no single manufacturer drawing; vendors differ by a millimetre and by which pads are present.
notes: GPIO9 strapped low enters the download bootloader. The onboard LED pin is not the same on every clone.

name: NodeMCU ESP8266 LoLin V3
description: ESP-12E module (ESP8266EX) with a CH340 USB-UART. 80 or 160 MHz, typically 4 MB flash, about 80 KB user RAM. Wi-Fi only. Micro-USB, 3.3 V logic, two 1×15 headers. The V3 board is longer than the Amica V2 (about 49 × 26 mm).

pins.name: D8
pins.fn: GPIO15, must be low at boot

pins.name: A0
pins.fn: ADC, about 0–1 V on the bare pin; the board divider accepts higher

notes: The linked PDF is the ESP8266EX chip datasheet. V3 outline varies slightly between LoLin batches.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico
description: RP2040, dual Cortex-M0+ at 133 MHz, 264 KB SRAM, 2 MB QSPI flash. 51 × 21 × 1.0 mm. 26 GPIO on a 40-pin castellated DIP, 3 of them ADC. Micro-USB. 3.3 V logic. VSYS accepts 1.8–5.5 V.
frame: Centre origin. Holes are symmetric (±23.5, ±5.7). +y is the pin 1–20 row; +x points from the SWD end toward the micro-USB end. Header x is treated as centred on the 48.26 mm pin span.
notes: Four 2.1 mm mounting holes. Pin holes are 1.0 mm on a 2.54 mm grid, rows 17.78 mm apart. GPIO is not 5 V tolerant.

name: Raspberry Pi Pico W
description: Pico plus an Infineon CYW43439 for 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi 4 and Bluetooth 5.2. Same 51 × 21 × 1.0 mm outline, 40-pin grid and mounting holes. The antenna sits at the end opposite the USB connector. 2 MB flash, RP2040.
frame: Centre origin. Holes are symmetric (±23.5, ±5.7). +y is the pin 1–20 row; +x points from the SWD end toward the micro-USB end. Header x is treated as centred on the 48.26 mm pin span.
notes: Keep copper and metal away from the antenna end. WL_GPIO on the CYW43439 is not on the edge pins. Operating range is narrower than the plain Pico when the radio is fitted (about −20 °C to +70 °C).

name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2
description: RP2350 on the Pico outline. Dual Cortex-M33 (or Hazard3 RISC-V) at 150 MHz, 520 KB SRAM, 4 MB flash. Pin-compatible with the original Pico: same 40-pin grid, same three ADC pins, micro-USB, no radio. 3.3 V logic.
frame: Centre origin. Holes are symmetric (±23.5, ±5.7). +y is the pin 1–20 row; +x points from the SWD end toward the micro-USB end. Header x is treated as centred on the 48.26 mm pin span.
notes: SKU is left as the product name. Raspberry Pi’s retail codes for Pico 2 have more than one revision and are easy to mix up.

name: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B 4GB
description: BCM2711, quad Cortex-A72 at 1.5 GHz, 4 GB LPDDR4. 85 × 56 mm, 40-pin HAT header, two micro-HDMI, USB-C power (5 V, 3 A supply recommended), Gigabit Ethernet, Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0. This is a Linux single-board computer, not a bare MCU.
frame: Centre origin on an 85 × 56 mm board. +x points toward the micro-HDMI / USB-C short edge (GPIO pin 1). −x points toward the Ethernet end. +y points toward the 40-pin header. Holes are the 58 × 49 mm pattern, drill 2.7 mm for M2.5.
notes: GPIO is 3.3 V. The 5 V pins can supply the board or be fed from it. 1 GB, 2 GB and 8 GB are the other RAM options (SC0193 is 2 GB, SC0195 is 8 GB).

name: Raspberry Pi 5 4GB
description: BCM2712, quad Cortex-A76 at 2.4 GHz, 4 GB LPDDR4X. Same 85 × 56 mm HAT footprint and 40-pin header as the Pi 4. USB-C power, 5 V at 5 A recommended when USB peripherals are attached, 3 A minimum. Dual micro-HDMI, PCIe FFC, RTC battery connector, power button. Wi-Fi 5 and Bluetooth 5.
frame: Centre origin on an 85 × 56 mm board. +x points toward the micro-HDMI / USB-C short edge (GPIO pin 1). −x points toward the Ethernet end. +y points toward the 40-pin header. Holes are the 58 × 49 mm pattern, drill 2.7 mm for M2.5.
notes: 8 GB boards sell for about $80. Retail SKUs changed across board spins, so the MPN is the product name. Mounting holes match the Pi 4 so existing HATs still fit; the port mix does not.

name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
description: RP3A0 (BCM2710A1), quad Cortex-A53 at 1 GHz, 512 MB RAM. 65 × 30 mm. Mini-HDMI, micro-USB OTG, micro-USB power, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, unpopulated 40-pin HAT header. The PCB has no M2.5 mounting holes.
frame: 65 × 30 mm. The 40-pin header runs along one long edge and is not fitted from the factory.
notes: A 5 V, 2.5 A supply is the usual recommendation. Camera uses the CSI connector.

name: STM32 Blue Pill
description: The common “Blue Pill” board: STM32F103C8T6, Cortex-M3 at 72 MHz, 64 KB flash, 20 KB SRAM, in an LQFP-48. Micro-USB, AMS1117-3.3, two rows of 20 pins. 3.3 V logic; many pins are 5 V tolerant. Clones differ in the USB pull-up and in the crystal.

pins.name: BOOT0
pins.fn: Boot from system memory when high

notes: C8 parts are often remarked and may be C6 (32 KB) silicon. SWD needs an external probe; the Micro-USB port is device-only and the ROM bootloader needs a specific pull-up.

name: STM32 Nucleo-F401RE
description: STM32F401RET6, Cortex-M4F at 84 MHz, 512 KB flash, 96 KB SRAM, on the MB1136 Nucleo-64 board. Arduino Uno R3 headers plus two 2×19 ST morpho headers. On-board ST-LINK/V2-1 on a snap-off section, USB Mini-B. 3.3 V logic; most pins are 5 V tolerant.

pins.name: D0
pins.fn: PA3 / USART2 RX, also the ST-LINK VCP

pins.name: VIN
pins.fn: 7–12 V when JP5 is on E5V

notes: User manual is UM1724. Outline is the figure usually quoted as about 82.5 × 70 mm including ST-LINK; confirm on the current drawing before a case. PC14/PC15 go to the 32.768 kHz crystal on later MB1136 revisions.

name: Teensy 4.1
description: NXP i.MX RT1062, Cortex-M7 at 600 MHz, 1024 KB RAM (512 KB tightly coupled), 8 MB flash. 61 × 17.8 mm. 3.3 V I/O, not 5 V tolerant. USB Micro-B device, USB host pads, microSD (SDIO), 10/100 Ethernet PHY (DP83825) that still needs a magjack. 42 breadboard I/O, 55 I/O total.
frame: 61.0 × 17.8 mm (PJRC 2.4 × 0.7 in). Micro-USB on one short end. No mounting holes.
notes: Outer header is not a single 24-pin row; PJRC breaks out 42 breadboard pins across both long edges plus the USB-host and Ethernet pads. Pin card is at pjrc.com/store/teensy41.html.

name: Adafruit Feather RP2040
description: Feather outline, 50.8 × 22.8 mm, RP2040 at about 125 MHz, 264 KB SRAM, 8 MB flash. USB-C, LiPo charger, STEMMA QT, 3.3 V logic. Four mounting holes. Assembled height is about 7 mm without headers; the PCB itself is 1.6 mm.
notes: Charger is the usual Feather LiPo circuit (about 200 mA or better, depending on the build). The linked PDF is the RP2040 datasheet, not the Feather guide. Hole coordinates are on the Adafruit fab print.

name: Seeed XIAO ESP32S3
description: XIAO outline, 21 × 17.5 mm. ESP32-S3 with 8 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE, USB-C, 3.3 V logic. 14 castellations: D0–D10 plus 5 V, GND and 3.3 V. Battery pads on the back. This is the plain board, not the Sense camera version.
notes: GPIO numbers follow the Seeed wiki mapping and are easy to confuse with the pad names. No mounting holes. Populated height is a few millimetres above the 1.6 mm PCB.

name: Adafruit KB2040
description: Pro Micro outline RP2040 board for keyboards. 33.0 × 17.8 mm PCB (Adafruit’s 1.3 × 0.7 in). 8 MB flash, 264 KB SRAM, USB-C, 3.3 V logic, STEMMA QT, NeoPixel, boot and reset buttons. Castellated pads. Some distributors quote 35 × 17.8 × 4.9 mm including the USB-C shell.

pins.name: RAW
pins.fn: VBUS after the fuse and diode, about 5 V

frame: Pro Micro footprint. Two rows of 12 castellations. USB-C on one short end, STEMMA QT on the other.
notes: 3.3 V only, unlike a 5 V Pro Micro. A bottom jumper bypasses the 500 mA fuse for USB host or high-current LEDs. GLB is served from /models/kb2040.glb.

name: ESP32-WROOM-32E-N8
description: Solder-down ESP32 module, PCB antenna, 8 MB flash. Dual-core LX6 at 240 MHz, 520 KB SRAM, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. 18.0 × 25.5 × 3.3 mm, 38 pads. This is the land pattern the studio module footprint was drawn for.
notes: Peak Wi-Fi current is several hundred milliamps. GPIO 34–39 are input-only. Flash pins IO6–IO11 are not free GPIO.

name: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R8
description: ESP32-S3 module, 8 MB flash and 8 MB octal PSRAM, PCB antenna. Dual LX7 at 240 MHz, 512 KB SRAM, USB, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE. Same 18 × 25.5 mm family outline as the WROOM-32E.
notes: Octal PSRAM occupies GPIO 35–37. The studio module footprint is the 38-pad WROOM-32E land, which is only a stand-in for the S3 pad map.

name: ESP32-C3-MINI-1
description: Small ESP32-C3 module, RISC-V at 160 MHz, 4 MB flash, 400 KB SRAM, PCB antenna, USB. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE. Much smaller than a WROOM; the studio still draws it with the WROOM body.
notes: Outline is the commonly quoted MINI-1 body and should be checked on the module drawing before a paste mask. The linked PDF is the C3 chip datasheet.

name: BME280 breakout
description: Humidity, pressure and temperature. The IC runs at 1.71–3.6 V and draws a few microamps between conversions; the usual GY breakout accepts 3.3 V or 5 V through an onboard regulator and speaks I2C (0x76 or 0x77) or SPI.

pins.name: VCC
pins.fn: 3.3 or 5 V on the usual breakout

pins.name: CSB
pins.fn: SPI chip select, pull up for I2C

pins.name: SDO
pins.fn: SPI SDO, also sets I2C address

notes: The linked PDF is the bare Bosch IC. Breakout PCB size varies; 15 × 12 mm is typical of the purple GY board.

name: BMP280 breakout
description: Pressure and temperature only, the cheaper sibling of the BME280. Same I2C addresses and the same 6-pin breakout pinout on most GY boards. No humidity.

pins.name: VCC
pins.fn: 3.3 or 5 V on the usual breakout

name: DHT22 / AM2302
description: Humidity and temperature on a single-wire protocol. 3.3–5.5 V, one reading about every 2 seconds. Body is 15.1 × 25 × 7.7 mm plus the leads. Needs a pull-up on the data pin, usually 10 kΩ.
notes: Not Dallas 1-Wire. Accuracy is about ±0.5 °C and ±2 % RH. The 3-pin footprint drops the NC lead.

name: SHT31-DIS breakout
description: Calibrated humidity and temperature, I2C at 0x44 or 0x45. The bare die is 2.5 × 2.5 mm and 2.4–5.5 V. Breakouts usually level-shift and regulate so a 3.3 V or 5 V host can talk to them.

pins.name: VIN
pins.fn: 2.4–5.5 V, or 3.3/5 V on a breakout

notes: Breakout outline is typical, not a Sensirion drawing. ADR pin strapped on many modules.

name: MPU-6050 breakout
description: 6-axis IMU: 3-axis accelerometer and 3-axis gyroscope, plus a temperature sensor. I2C address 0x68 (AD0 low) or 0x69. The IC is 2.375–3.46 V; GY-521 breakouts accept 3.3 V or 5 V.

pins.name: XDA
pins.fn: Aux I2C data, for an external magnetometer

notes: GY-521 PCBs are commonly about 21 × 16 mm. The IC itself is a 4 × 4 mm QFN-24.

name: ICM-20948 breakout
description: 9-axis IMU: accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer, plus a DMP. I2C (0x68/0x69) or SPI. 1.71–3.6 V on the IC. The practical successor when an MPU-6050 is not enough.

pins.name: VIN
pins.fn: 3.3 V, or 5 V if the breakout regulates

name: BNO055 breakout
description: 9-axis absolute-orientation sensor with on-chip sensor fusion, so the host reads a quaternion or Euler angles instead of calibrating a filter. I2C (0x28 or 0x29) or UART. IC supply 2.4–3.6 V.
notes: Needs a short calibration move. Generic modules are cheaper than the Adafruit board and not always well regulated. Outline is a typical breakout.

name: VL53L0X breakout
description: Time-of-flight distance sensor. The datasheet range is about 30 mm to 2 m; indoors, against a typical target, it is useful to around 1.2 m. I2C, default 0x29. The IC is 2.6–3.5 V; breakouts often accept 3.3–5 V.

pins.name: XSHUT
pins.fn: Shutdown, also used to change the address

notes: Cover the sensor window with nothing but the specified cover glass. Outline is a typical breakout, not the 4.4 × 2.4 mm optical LGA.

name: HC-SR04 ultrasonic
description: Ultrasonic ranger, about 2 cm to 4 m. Trigger and echo are 5 V pulses; echo into a 3.3 V MCU needs a divider. Two transducers on a 45 × 20 mm board. 5 V supply, about 15 mA while ranging.

pins.name: Echo
pins.fn: Pulse width is the round trip, 5 V

notes: There is no single manufacturer. A 3.3 V-tolerant variant is sold as RCWL-1601 or HC-SR04P; this entry is the common 5 V board.

name: HC-SR501 PIR
description: Passive infrared motion detector. 4.5–20 V supply, digital output that swings high when it sees motion. Two trimmers set sensitivity and hold time. Repeat-trigger jumper.
notes: Quiescent current is tens of microamps; 0.05 mA is the idle figure, not the output drive. Lens height makes the module about 25 mm tall. Output high is about 3.3 V on most boards.

name: INA219 breakout
description: High-side current and voltage monitor, I2C, 0–26 V bus. INA219AIDCNR is the SOT-23-8 part. GY breakouts use a 0.1 Ω shunt and report current, bus voltage and power. Addresses 0x40–0x4F.
notes: With the usual 0.1 Ω shunt the full-scale current is ±3.2 A before the PGA is changed. Outline is the common blue breakout.

name: ACS712 current module
description: Hall-effect current sensor. The -05B is ±5 A at 185 mV/A, the -20A is 100 mV/A and the -30A is 66 mV/A. 5 V supply. Isolated, but the module terminals are at line potential if you wire them that way.
notes: Output is not safe to feed straight into a 3.3 V ADC at the top of the range. The SOIC-8 IC is what Allegro sells; this entry is the usual 5 A module. Bandwidth is about 80 kHz.

name: DS18B20
description: Dallas 1-Wire temperature sensor, −55 °C to +125 °C, ±0.5 °C from −10 °C to +85 °C. 3.0–5.5 V, or parasite power from the data line. TO-92. Waterproof probe cables use the same IC.

pins.name: DQ
pins.fn: Pin 2, 1-Wire data, needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up

pins.name: VDD
pins.fn: Pin 3, supply, or tie handling for parasite power

notes: Active conversion is about 1 mA for under a second; idle is about 1 µA. Many cheap probes are counterfeit and fail the family-code check.

name: MAX30102 breakout
description: Pulse oximeter and heart-rate sensor, red and IR LEDs with a photodetector. I2C at 0x57. 1.8 V core and 3.3 V LED supply on the IC; breakouts usually take 3.3 V or 5 V and regulate both.
notes: LED current is configurable and dominates the draw. Cover the glass with a finger, not a gap. Outline is a typical purple breakout.

name: ADS1115 breakout
description: 16-bit delta-sigma ADC, 4 single-ended channels or 2 differential, PGA from ±0.256 V to ±6.144 V, I2C. Up to 860 SPS. Address 0x48–0x4B. The VSSOP-10 IC is 2.0–5.5 V.
notes: Inputs must stay inside the supply. A ±6.144 V PGA range does not make the pin 6 V tolerant. Breakout outline is typical.

name: TCS34725 breakout
description: RGB and clear-light sensor with an IR blocking filter and a white LED on most breakouts. I2C at 0x29. 3.3 V logic. Useful for colour sorting, not for display calibration.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.fn: Regulated 3.3 V out on many boards

notes: The LED can draw more than the sensor. Outline is a typical breakout.

name: GY-NEO6M GPS
description: u-blox NEO-6M GPS module on the common GY board with a ceramic antenna and a backup coin cell or supercap. UART, default 9600 baud, NMEA. 3.3 V logic. The module RF input is 50 Ω if you swap the antenna.
notes: Cold start can take a minute with a clear sky. TX/RX are 3.3 V even when VCC is 5 V. Board outline includes the patch antenna and varies.

name: SG90 micro servo
description: 9 g hobby servo, about 0–180°. 4.8–6 V. Running current is typically under 200 mA; stall is roughly 500–700 mA. Control is a 50 Hz pulse, about 1–2 ms. Body about 22.8 × 12.2 × 22.5 mm; the mounting ears span about 32 mm.

pins.name: PWM
pins.fn: Orange or yellow, 50 Hz servo pulse

notes: Do not power a servo from a USB 3.3 V regulator. The header is the connector you put on the PCB, not the servo body.

name: 28BYJ-48 stepper
description: Unipolar geared stepper, usually the 5 V winding. About 64 steps per revolution at the rotor and a gearbox near 64:1, so about 4096 half-steps per output revolution. Drive it with the ULN2003 board. Five-wire cable.
notes: 12 V versions exist and look identical. The ear-to-ear mounting span is about 35 mm. Gear ratio is nominal, not exact.

name: TT gear motor 1:48
description: Yellow dual-shaft hobby gear motor, 1:48 reduction, about 200 rpm at 6 V. Running current about 150–250 mA, stall over 1 A. Ships with a 65 mm wheel on most kits.

name: N20 micro gear motor 100 rpm
description: Metal-gear micro motor, 12 × 10 mm can, about 100 rpm at 6 V. Running current about 60–100 mA, stall about 0.5 A. Compact rovers and small robots.

name: JGA25-370 gear motor 12 V
description: 25 mm metal gearmotor, 12 V, about 280 rpm. Running current about 300 mA, stall around 2 A — check the driver peak rating. Heavier rovers.

name: ULN2003 stepper driver board
description: The red board sold with the 28BYJ-48: a ULN2003A Darlington array, four LEDs and a 5-pin motor socket. Each channel is rated 500 mA. Logic in is 5 V. The DIP or SOIC ULN2003A is the chip on this board.

pins.name: VCC
pins.fn: Motor supply, 5 V for the usual 28BYJ-48

notes: The IC has internal clamp diodes to the COM pin; COM must go to the motor supply. Board outline varies.

name: A4988 stepper module
description: Bipolar stepper driver on the Pololu-style 15.2 × 20.3 mm carrier. Motor supply about 8–35 V, logic 3.3 V or 5 V. Up to 1/16 microstepping. Set the current with the trimpot; about 1 A continuous without a heatsink, 2 A peak with cooling.

pins.name: VMOT
pins.fn: Motor supply, with a bulk capacitor

notes: Put at least 100 µF across VMOT at the module. Logic current is the 10 mA figure; motor current is separate.

name: DRV8825 stepper module
description: Bipolar stepper driver, same 15.2 × 20.3 mm carrier as the A4988 and a similar pinout. 8.2–45 V motor supply, up to 1/32 microstepping. About 1.5 A continuous without extra cooling, 2.2 A peak.
notes: The trimpot equation is not the same as the A4988. Do not drop one in for the other without resetting the current.

name: TMC2209 SilentStepStick
description: StealthChop / SpreadCycle stepper driver with UART configuration. Same general 15 × 20 mm stick outline. Motor supply up to 29 V, about 2 A RMS with cooling. Logic 3.3 V or 5 V. Much quieter than an A4988.
notes: Pin names on BigTreeTech and Fysetc sticks are not identical. Index is up to 256 microsteps internally; the STEP pin usually sees 1/16.

name: TB6612FNG
description: Dual H-bridge, 1.2 A per channel continuous, about 3.2 A peak, motor supply 4.5–13.5? V (15 V absolute on many prints) and logic 2.7–5.5 V. SSOP-24, which matches the studio ssop footprint.

pins.name: STBY
pins.fn: Standby, must be high to run

notes: STBY low puts the outputs in high-Z. VM max is often listed as 15 V absolute and about 13.5 V recommended. Confirm on the Toshiba sheet before a 15 V design.

name: L298N motor module
description: Dual H-bridge module built on the L298N. 5–35 V motor supply, 5 V logic. About 2 A peak per bridge and a large dropout, so a 12 V motor sees closer to 10 V. Onboard 5 V regulator enabled by a jumper when VM is under about 12 V.

pins.name: 5V
pins.fn: Logic 5 V, in or out depending on the jumper

notes: Quiescent of the bare IC is high (tens of milliamps). The module’s screw-terminal block is the part the terminal footprint stands in for.

name: DRV8833 breakout
description: Dual H-bridge, 1.5 A per channel peak, motor supply 2.7–10.8 V, logic down to 1.8 V so it is happy on 3.3 V. The usual breakout is a small carrier with current-limit pots or a solder jumper, not the QFN itself.
notes: Continuous current is closer to 1 A with copper and less on a tiny breakout. Outline is a typical carrier.

name: 1-channel relay module
description: 5 V coil relay on a module with a transistor, flyback diode and screw terminals. Contacts are usually rated 10 A at 250 VAC / 30 VDC on the silkscreen; treat cheap modules as 7–10 A and keep mains off a logic PCB. Active-low trigger on most boards.
notes: Coil current is about 70 mA. The terminal footprint represents the COM/NO/NC block. Opto-isolated versions need the JD-VCC jumper removed and a separate coil supply.

name: IRLZ44N
description: Logic-level N-channel MOSFET in TO-220. 55 V, low Rds(on) at 4–5 V gate (tens of milliohms). Usable as a 5 V low-side switch. At 3.3 V the gate is only partly enhanced; check the curve before a high-current 3.3 V design.
notes: The tab is drain. A 100–220 Ω series gate resistor and a 100 kΩ gate-source pulldown are the usual circuit. The sot223 footprint is only a visual stand-in. Continuous current is package- and heatsink-limited, not the 47 A headline.

name: SSD1306 0.96" OLED
description: 128 × 64 monochrome OLED. The common 4-pin board is I2C at 0x3C or 0x3D, 3.3 V logic, and usually accepts 3.3 V or 5 V on VCC. Panel current is typically under 20 mA with a sparse image.
notes: 7-pin modules expose SPI (D0, D1, RES, DC, CS) instead of, or as well as, I2C. Outline is the usual square I2C board.

name: SH1106 1.3" OLED
description: 128 × 64 OLED, 1.3 inch, usually I2C. The RAM is 132 × 64, so a driver written for SSD1306 needs a 2-column offset or the image sits off to one side. 3.3 V logic.

name: ST7789 1.54" TFT
description: 240 × 240 IPS TFT, SPI. Logic 3.3 V. The usual module has a microSD slot that shares the SPI bus. Backlight is a separate LED pin, often happy at 3.3 V through a resistor.
notes: Init sequences differ between panels (offset and RGB order). Outline is a typical 1.54 inch module.

name: ST7789 2.0" TFT
description: 240 × 320 TFT on the same ST7789 controller as the 1.54 inch panel, SPI, 3.3 V logic. Different glass offset, so the init table is not interchangeable.

name: ILI9341 2.8" TFT
description: 240 × 320 SPI TFT, the common 2.8 inch module with a touch controller (often XPT2046) and a microSD slot on the same SPI bus. Logic is 3.3 V. Touch and the panel need separate chip selects.

pins.name: VCC
pins.fn: 3.3 V, some boards have a regulator

notes: A 5 V Arduino needs level shifting on CS, DC, RST, MOSI and SCK. Outline is a typical module and the header is often 14 pins.

name: 1602 HD44780 LCD
description: 16 × 2 character LCD, parallel 4-bit or 8-bit bus. 5 V. Outline 80 × 36 mm, viewing area about 64.5 × 16 mm. Contrast pin (VO) wants a 10 kΩ pot to ground. Backlight is a separate LED, about 20 mA.

pins.name: RW
pins.fn: Read / write, tie low to write only

frame: Centre of the 80 × 36 mm outline. Holes follow the common 75 × 31 mm pattern and should be checked on the panel drawing.
notes: Logic current is about 1–2 mA. Backlight is extra. Hole positions are the usual drawing, not a measurement of one panel.

name: PCF8574
description: 8-bit I2C expander, the chip on a 1602 backpack. Address 0x20–0x27 (PCF8574A is 0x38–0x3F). 2.5–6 V, 100 kHz. SOIC-16, which matches the studio soic footprint. Quasi-bidirectional pins, about 20–25 mA sink.
notes: SOIC-16 body is about 10.3 × 7.5 mm including leads in the wide view; the moulded body is narrower. A backpack module is the usual way this meets a 1602, and it maps P0–P7 onto RS, RW, E, backlight and the data nibbles.

name: WS2812B
description: Addressable RGB LED in a 5.0 × 5.0 mm package. 5 V supply, one data line at 800 kHz. Each LED draws about 1 mA idle and up to about 50–60 mA at full white. Chain DIN to the previous DOUT.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.fn: Data out to the next LED

notes: A 3.3 V GPIO is marginal. Use a 74HCT125 or similar, a 330–470 Ω series resistor on DIN, and a bulk capacitor at the strip. The led footprint is a 0603 stand-in, not a 5050 land.

name: WS2812B strip, 60 LED/m
description: 1 metre of 60 LED/m WS2812B strip, IP30 (bare flex). 5 V, 3-wire (5 V, data, ground). Full-white budget is about 60 × 50 mA = 3 A per metre. Inject power at both ends on longer runs.

pins.name: DIN
pins.fn: Data, arrow points away from the controller

notes: currentMa is idle-ish for the metre, not full white. IP65 and IP67 sleeves change the width. Cut only on the marked pads.

name: MAX7219 8×8 matrix
description: 8×8 LED matrix module driven by a MAX7219. SPI-like serial (DIN, CS, CLK), 5 V. Modules daisy-chain. The IC can also drive eight 7-segment digits. The 8×8 block is 32 × 32 mm.
notes: Set the scan limit and the intensity register or the display looks random. A 4-in-1 module is four of these cascaded. Peak current depends on how many LEDs are lit.

name: 2.9" e-paper module
description: 2.9 inch black-and-white e-paper, typically 296 × 128, SPI. The panel only draws current while refreshing (a second or two) and then holds the image. 3.3 V logic. Busy pin must be honoured. Many modules follow the Waveshare pinout.
notes: Red/black and 4-gray panels share the size and not the init code. Refresh current is higher than the 5 mA idle figure, often tens of milliamps. Outline is a typical module.

name: nRF24L01+
description: 2.4 GHz transceiver, SPI, 250 kbps to 2 Mbps, 3.3 V only. The small PCB-antenna module is about 29 × 15 mm. A 5 V data pin can damage it. The PA+LNA version with the external antenna draws far more current and needs a solid 3.3 V rail.
notes: 13 mA is a typical TX at 0 dBm. Put 10 µF or more on VCC at the module. Decoupling is the usual reason a link is flaky.

name: RFM95W LoRa
description: HopeRF module built on the Semtech SX1276. 868/915 MHz LoRa, SPI, 3.3 V, up to +20 dBm. The module is 16 × 16 mm. A 5 V SPI bus needs shifting. Antenna is 50 Ω.
notes: 120 mA is the +20 dBm transmit figure. Receive is closer to 12 mA. Use the frequency the module was tuned for. The module footprint is the WROOM stand-in, larger than 16 mm.

name: HC-05 Bluetooth module
description: Bluetooth 2.0 SPP module, UART, default 9600 baud in data mode and 38400 in AT mode. 3.6–6 V on the breakout KEY/EN pin board; the radio itself is 3.3 V. Not BLE. Useful as a wireless serial cable.
notes: RXD on a 5 V Arduino should be divided. The bare 27 × 13 mm module without the baseboard is 3.3 V only. Outline here is the 6-pin breakout.

name: MCP2515 CAN module
description: CAN 2.0B controller, SPI, usually paired with a TJA1050 transceiver on a blue breakout. 8 MHz or 16 MHz crystal — the driver must match. Bus is differential CANH/CANL. Logic 2.7–5.5 V. Terminate the bus with 120 Ω at each end.
notes: The IC is SOIC-18. Many modules are 5 V only because of the TJA1050. Crystal frequency is printed on the can.

name: W5500 Ethernet module
description: Hardwired TCP/IP Ethernet controller, SPI, 3.3 V, integrated PHY. The common module includes the RJ45 magjack. Up to 80 MHz SPI. 32 KB buffer. Much less software than an ENC28J60.
notes: 130 mA is a busy-link ballpark. Some breakouts accept 5 V and regulate. The bare W5500 is a 48-pin LQFP. Outline includes a typical magjack module.

name: SIM800L
description: Quad-band GSM/GPRS module, UART AT commands. Supply is 3.4–4.4 V, not 5 V. Transmit bursts reach about 2 A, so it wants a low-impedance source and a large capacitor, typically a LiPo or a beefy buck. The red core board is about 25 × 23 mm.
notes: currentMa is a call-mode average, not the 2 A burst. Antenna must be fitted before transmitting. 2G networks are gone in many countries.

name: CH340C
description: USB full-speed to UART bridge with an internal oscillator, so no crystal. SOIC-16, which matches the studio soic footprint. 5 V or 3.3 V. The C variant is the one used when the board should not need a 12 MHz crystal.

pins.name: DTR
pins.fn: Often wired to EN through a capacitor for auto-reset

pins.name: RTS
pins.fn: Often wired to GPIO0 for auto-boot

notes: CH340G needs the crystal; CH340C does not. Body length is about 10 mm.

name: CP2102
description: USB-to-UART bridge, QFN-28, internal oscillator and regulator. 3.0–3.6 V I/O when self-powered from USB, or an external 3.3 V rail. Drivers are in mainline OS images. The studio draws it as an SOIC stand-in.
notes: CP2102N is the newer drop-in family and is often the one actually in stock. The linked PDF covers CP2102 and CP2109.

name: AMS1117-3.3
description: 1 A low-dropout linear regulator, 3.3 V fixed, SOT-223. Dropout is about 1.1 V at 800 mA, so the input wants about 4.5 V or more. Quiescent current is roughly 5–10 mA. Needs capacitors on input and output; many clones want a tantalum or a low-ESR part on the output to stay stable.
notes: Tab is VOUT on the fixed AMS1117, not ground. 800 mA is a practical PCB current; 1 A needs copper as a heatsink. Dropout and max input vary by clone.

name: LM2596 buck module
description: Adjustable buck module, about 4–40 V in and 1.25–35 V out, commonly sold as a 3 A converter. Realistic continuous current on the small blue board is closer to 2 A without a fan. About 150 kHz. Adjustable trimpot.
notes: Many boards are remarked clones. Set the pot before connecting a load. currentMa is quiescent, not load current.

name: MP1584 buck module
description: Small adjustable buck, 4.5–28 V in, down to about 0.8 V out, 1.5 MHz. The chip is 3 A peak; the tiny module is happy around 1–2 A. Much smaller than an LM2596 board.
notes: EN pin is usually tied on. Outline is the common mini module.

name: TP4056 charger module
description: Linear 1S LiPo charger. USB in, BAT± out. The usual module sets 1 A with a 1.2 kΩ PROG resistor. Red charging, blue done. Do not charge above 4.2 V and do not omit a protection circuit if the cell does not have one. Some boards include DW01 protection.

pins.name: OUT+
pins.fn: Protected output, on boards that have DW01

notes: The chip is SOP-8. 1 A into a small cell is aggressive; raise PROG if the cell is under about 500 mAh. Outline is the common Micro-USB board.

name: MT3608 boost module
description: Adjustable boost, 2–24 V in, up to about 28 V out. The chip is rated 2 A switch current, so available output current falls as the boost ratio rises. Fine for 5 V to 12 V at a few hundred milliamps.
notes: ioutMa is a practical 5-to-12 V figure, not the switch rating. The pot is sensitive at the top of the range.

name: XL6009 boost module
description: Boost (and on some boards buck-boost) module, about 5–32 V in and up to about 35 V out. Higher current than an MT3608 at the cost of a larger inductor. 400 kHz class. The common red board is in the same size class as an LM2596 module.
notes: Switch current rating is often quoted as 4 A. Output current is less. Set the pot before connecting a 5 V load.

name: 18650 cell holder
description: Single 18650 through-hole holder, two pins. The cell is 18.6 mm diameter by about 65 mm. A holder is roughly 77 × 21 mm. An unprotected 18650 still needs a protection circuit or a charger that limits 4.2 V and current.
notes: Nominal cell voltage is 3.6–3.7 V. Discharge cutoff is about 3.0 V. Holder length varies with the spring.

name: 1S LiPo JST-PH lead
description: 2-pin JST PH plug (2.00 mm) on a 1S LiPo pigtail. Housing is PHR-2; the PCB mate is S2B-PH-K-S or a top-entry B2B-PH-K-S. 3.7 V nominal, 4.2 V full, about 3.0 V empty. Polarity is not universal: check red against the silk.
notes: PH is 2.0 mm. Do not mate it with a 2.5 mm XH plug. A 26 AWG lead is comfortable around 1–2 A.

name: microSD SPI module
description: SPI microSD breakout. 3.3 V card with a level shifter and often an AMS1117 so the header can be 5 V. CS, MOSI, MISO, SCK. Not an SDIO socket. Cards want a short SPI and solid ground.

pins.name: VCC
pins.fn: 5 V or 3.3 V, read the silk

notes: Some boards are 3.3 V only and will be damaged by 5 V logic. Write current is higher than 30 mA.

name: W25Q128JV
description: 128 Mbit (16 MB) SPI NOR flash, 2.7–3.6 V, SOIC-8 208 mil. Standard SPI, Dual and Quad. About 15 mA while reading, under 1 µA in power-down. The usual external flash next to an ESP32 or a bootloader.
notes: The studio soic footprint is a 16-pin body, so this is a stand-in. JVSIQ is the 208 mil industrial part. Quad mode needs WP and HOLD as IO.

name: AT24C256
description: 256 Kbit (32 KB) I2C EEPROM, SOIC-8. 1.7–5.5 V on the C revision. 32-byte page writes. Address 0x50–0x57 from A0–A2. About 1 million write cycles, 100 years retention on the datasheet.
notes: SOIC-8 is narrower than the 16-pin soic drawing. A 1.7 V minimum applies to the C die; older AT24C256 is 2.5 V.

name: 6×6 mm tactile switch
description: 6 × 6 mm tactile switch, the part the studio tact footprint draws. Common heights 4.3–7 mm. About 50 mA at 12 V contact rating. Four pads, two pairs. Used for RESET and BOOT.
notes: Through-hole and SMD versions share the 6 × 6 body. The footprint in the studio is the SMD land.

name: EC11 rotary encoder
description: Incremental encoder with a push switch. Typically 20 detents and 20 pulses per revolution. 5 V contact rating is fine at 3.3 V with pull-ups. Needs debounce or a state machine, not a single edge interrupt.
notes: Vertical and right-angle bodies differ. 12–14 mm is the body under a panel bushing, not the shaft length. Many are 20 or 30 detents.

name: KY-023 joystick
description: Dual 10 kΩ potentiometer thumbstick with a push switch. Two analog axes and one digital click. 3.3 V or 5 V. Axes rest near mid-rail and should be calibrated.

pins.name: SW
pins.fn: Switch, active low, needs a pull-up

notes: Height includes the stick. PCB is the 34 × 26 mm part.

name: 4×4 membrane keypad
description: 16-key membrane keypad, 8 pins: 4 rows and 4 columns. Scan by driving one row and reading columns. About 69 × 77 mm. Contacts are a few hundred ohms when pressed.
notes: Row and column order is printed on the tail and is not the same on every vendor. Outline is the common membrane.

name: TTP223 touch module
description: Capacitive touch pad. The module output goes high (or toggles, depending on the A/B pads) when a finger is near. 2.0–5.5 V. No mechanical travel. Sensitive to ground pours directly under the pad.
notes: Idle current is on the order of 10 µA. The SOT-23-6 IC is smaller than the module. Outline is a typical red board.

name: MAX98357A I2S amp
description: Filterless Class-D mono amp with an I2S input. 2.5–5.5 V. About 3 W into 4 Ω at 5 V, less into 8 Ω and less at 3.3 V. Gain pin selects 3, 6, 9, 12 or 15 dB. No MCLK required.
notes: 5 mA is idle. A loud 4 Ω speaker at 5 V is hundreds of milliamps. The TQFN is 3 × 3 mm; the outline is a typical breakout. Do not tie speaker pins to ground.

name: Passive buzzer
description: Magnetic transducer without an oscillator. Drive it with a square wave, often near 2 kHz, from a GPIO or a transistor. A 12 mm part is the common one. Silent if you only set the pin high.
notes: TMB12A05 is a representative 12 mm, 5 V magnetic buzzer family; the exact resonant frequency is printed on the part. 30 mA is a typical drive, not a precision figure.

name: Active buzzer
description: Buzzer with the oscillator inside. DC on, it sounds; DC off, it stops. Usually 5 V, about 2.3–2.7 kHz. A 12 mm body. Do not PWM it expecting a tone change.
notes: Current is about 20–30 mA. Polarity matters, unlike many passive transducers.

name: INMP441 I2S mic
description: Bottom-port MEMS microphone with an I2S output. 1.8–3.3 V. 24-bit, left or right channel selected by the L/R pin. Needs BCLK, WS and a controller that can be I2S master. Not PDM.
notes: The bare mic is a tiny LGA. This entry is the breakout. Do not put 5 V on VDD. 1.4 mA is the typical operating current of the mic.

name: 1N4148W switching diode
description: 100 V small-signal diode in SOD-123, the SMD form of the 1N4148. Continuous forward current is about 150 mA; peak is higher for a short pulse. The axial DO-35 1N4148 is the through-hole alternate. Drawn as an 0805 chip.
notes: Axial 1N4148 is documented at https://www.vishay.com/docs/81857/1n4148.pdf. This row is the SOD-123 part, not that DO-35 body. Vr 75 V on some 1N4148W bins and 100 V on the Diodes Inc datasheet; 100 V is used here.

name: SS34 Schottky
description: SMA Schottky, 40 V, 3 A. Use it as a buck catch diode or a reverse-protection diode where a 1N4148 would overheat. The studio draws an 0805 chip; the real land is an SMA (DO-214AC) pad, about 4.5 × 2.8 mm.

name: 1N5819 Schottky
description: Axial Schottky, DO-41, 40 V, 1 A. The through-hole companion to the SS34. Forward drop is about 0.4 V at a few hundred milliamps. Drawn as a chip stand-in.

name: 2N7002 N-MOSFET
description: SOT-23 N-channel MOSFET, 60 V. The small-signal switch for a relay, a buzzer, or a logic-level load under a couple of hundred milliamps. Continuous current depends on the vendor and the copper; plan on about 115 mA and read the datasheet if the load is larger. Drawn as an SOT-223 stand-in.
notes: Vgs(th) is about 2.1 V typical. A 3.3 V GPIO turns it on for light loads. Some second-source 2N7002 parts claim 200 mA or more.

name: BSS138 N-MOSFET
description: SOT-23 N-channel, 50 V, about 200 mA. The usual MOSFET in a discrete I2C level shifter (one device per line, gate at the low-side rail). Drawn as an SOT-223 stand-in.

pins.name: 2 S
pins.fn: Source, the low-voltage side in a shifter

name: AO3400 N-MOSFET
description: SOT-23 N-channel, 30 V. Rds(on) is roughly 30 mΩ at 10 V and about 50 mΩ at 4.5 V, so a 3.3 V GPIO can switch a couple of amps if the copper can take the heat. The silicon limit is 5.7 A; a small pad will not. Drawn as an SOT-223 stand-in.
notes: 2 A is a practical PCB current, not the 5.7 A datasheet pulse rating.

name: 8 MHz crystal 3225
description: 3.2 × 2.5 mm SMD crystal, 8.000 MHz, typically 12 pF load. ABM8G is the Abracon 3225 family; the full order code adds load, tolerance and packing. Drawn as an 0805 chip. A 4-pad land uses pads 1 and 3 for the crystal.

name: 12 MHz crystal 3225
description: 3.2 × 2.5 mm crystal, 12.000 MHz, typically 12 pF. Common USB full-speed clock. Confirm the Abracon load-capacitance suffix. Drawn as an 0805 chip.

name: 16 MHz crystal 3225
description: 3.2 × 2.5 mm crystal, 16.000 MHz, typically 12 pF. The ATmega328P and a lot of USB MCUs use this. Confirm the load suffix. Drawn as an 0805 chip.

name: 32.768 kHz crystal
description: Watch crystal, 32.768 kHz, 3.2 × 1.5 mm, typically 12.5 pF. Used for an RTC. The load-capacitance letter in the Abracon code is the digit to confirm. Drawn as an 0805 chip; the real land is two pads on a 3215 body.

name: 0603 ferrite bead 600 Ω
description: 0603 ferrite, 600 Ω at 100 MHz. Series element on a noisy 3.3 V or USB rail. Rated current is a few hundred milliamps and depends on the impedance curve and the allowed temperature rise; use the Murata plot instead of a single amp number.

name: USB-C 16-pin receptacle

name: PTC 1206 0.5 A
description: Resettable PTC, Bourns Multifuse 1206, 6 V, 0.50 A hold. The NSMF number is the hold current in hundredths of an amp, matching the 1.10 A NSMF110 code in the same 1206 family. Right for a USB VBUS rail, not for 12 V.
notes: Drawn as an 0805 chip. Hold current falls as temperature rises. Trip current is higher than 0.50 A.

name: PTC 1812 1.1 A
description: Resettable PTC, Bourns Multifuse 1812, 6 V, 1.1 A hold, about 2.2 A trip. Body about 4.7 × 3.4 × 0.85 mm. A USB source fuse when 0.5 A is too small. Not a 12 V part.
notes: Drawn as an 0805 chip. The 1812 land is larger.

name: Fuse 1206 1 A
description: One-time 1206 fast-acting fuse, 1 A, Littelfuse 0451 series. Unlike the PTCs above it does not reset. Confirm the voltage rating and the reel suffix on the current datasheet; 32 V is a safe planning number and several 0451 codes are rated higher.
notes: Drawn as an 0805 chip.

name: USBLC6-2SC6
description: USB 2.0 low-capacitance TVS array, SOT-23-6. Two data lines plus VBUS, all clamped to ground. Put it next to the connector. The studio draws an SOT-223 stand-in; the real package is SOT-23-6.
notes: Line capacitance is a few picofarads; use the datasheet figure rather than a remembered one. VBUS standoff is 5.25 V.
